messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A removable sensor bracket on a test rig. one fastener feels slightly loose but readings remain normal. You can intervene now or keep watching it. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "the loose fastener catches. i tap the bracket with one hand, then put the other on the bracket and listen for the tick. “yes,” i say, though the reading keeps changing. “maybe I left the bracket loose.”"}, {"id": "R014", "response": "I tighten the fastener and listen. I tap the bracket once, then again. I ease the bracket past the loose fastener and tighten it once more. I tap the bracket twice and leave it there."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "i keep the fastener beside it and leave the loose fastener visible. i run it once with a pencil mark on the bracket, then i leave the bracket loose for one short test. if the loose fastener catches, i mark the new mark and leave the fastener in place. if the reading stays normal, i keep the fastener in place and leave the loose fastener beside it."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "I press the bracket with my thumb, then leave it alone for one short run. I run it against the shaft, then leave it beside the rig. If the click stays steady, I mark the loose bracket with grease and leave it beside the rig."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "I rub my palm, then put the bracket on the bench edge. \"loose feels loose,\" I say. I scrape the bracket's edge once, then look at the readings. I keep my finger still. I mark the loose bracket with my thumbnail and try once more."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "I put the bracket back on the board. The loose fastener comes out. I put the bracket back on. The normal reading stays. I look at the rig. The bracket was wrong. I put the loose fastener back where it came."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "I press the bracket with my thumb, but the loose end slips. I tap the bracket with my heel, but the loose end catches on the gear. I keep watching until the sensor clicks. I leave the bracket seated and test the gear with a folded strip of paper."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "I turn the bracket once between finger and thumb. The loose edge catches. I press it with my thumbnail, then leave the rest of the reading alone. The fastener stays in place."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i press the bracket once with my thumbnail, then stop. the loose fastener stays. i move it to the back of the rig and keep a small note beside it."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i leave the fastener loose for one second and mark the bracket’s position with pencil. i move it once, then i put it under the same test load. if the loose bracket still catches, i keep the fastener in place and wait for the next test."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "i put the fastener on the bench and wait for the loose one to move. the bracket clicks. i put the fastener back on the bench. the loose one stays. i check the reading on the other piece. the bracket stays."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "\" loose. fastener. not here.\" You check the bracket's edge. \" Likely. slow.\" You turn the sensor upside down and inspect the loose fastener."}]
